Project Details – Outpost Odyssey
Team CODE ALCHEMIST | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

What does it do and how does it work?

Outpost Odyssey is an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Students take command of a small Moon or Mars outpost and manage four competing systems: life support (oxygen and water), radiation shielding, power, and food production.

Players choose destination, crew size, mission duration and difficulty, then advance day by day. They allocate limited resources, respond to training emergencies (solar radiation alerts, power faults, oxygen leaks, dust storms, etc.), and receive an explainable debrief at the end. A deterministic simulation engine calculates every resource change. An optional AI Mission Coach (powered by Gemini, with offline fallback) explains trade-offs and options but never changes the numbers or scores.

What benefits does it have?

  • Turns abstract space concepts into tangible decisions students can feel
  • Shows why life support, power, shielding and food compete for the same limited resources
  • Provides immediate, visible consequences for every choice
  • Includes NASA source citations and a clear “Simulation Assumptions” panel so learners understand what is real data versus educational simplification
  • Works fully offline for the core game; AI coach is optional

What is the intended impact?

To help young learners experience the real trade-offs of human space exploration in a safe, engaging way. Instead of only reading facts, students practice the kind of resource and risk decisions astronauts and mission planners face, building deeper understanding and curiosity about space STEM careers.

Tools, languages and software used

  • Language: Python
  • Framework: Streamlit (web interface)
  • Data & visualisation: NumPy, Pandas, Plotly
  • AI: Google Gemini API (with rule-based offline fallback)
  • Other: python-dotenv, Requests, Pytest
  • Version control: GitHub
  • No special hardware required — runs on any ordinary laptop

How is the project creative?

Most educational space tools are either too simplified (just facts) or too complex (professional software). Outpost Odyssey sits in the middle: a playable mission-control loop where four systems actively compete, emergencies force hard choices, and an AI coach explains options without giving magic answers. The combination of deterministic simulation, visible trade-offs, explainable debrief and responsible NASA grounding is distinctive.

Factors the team considered

  • Keeping the core experience complete and playable within a short hackathon window
  • Making every number and event clearly labelled as educational (not operational advice)
  • Ensuring the app still works if the AI or internet fails
  • Designing for ordinary student laptops and short play sessions
  • Honest use of NASA sources with full provenance (title, URL, use and limits)
  • Clear separation of roles so six first-year students could build in parallel and still integrate successfully

Educational concept. Not an official NASA product.
